faqs.question: What makes Trinity Pump & Supply different from a standard relaxation spa massage?
faqs.answer: Trinity Pump & Supply focuses on how tight muscles, fascial restrictions, and stubborn knots affect the way you move and feel. Instead of using light pressure mainly for relaxation, sessions apply targeted techniques to deeper soft tissue and restricted areas. The goal is to improve movement, reduce muscular tension, and support better day-to-day function.

faqs.question: Is deep tissue or muscle therapy supposed to be painful?
faqs.answer: Deep tissue work can create firm pressure and controlled therapeutic discomfort, especially around sensitive knots or restricted tissue. It should not feel sharp, burning, electrical, or unbearable. Your therapist adjusts pressure based on your response, so communication during treatment helps keep the work effective without pushing beyond a safe, manageable level.

faqs.question: How many sessions will I need to see noticeable pain relief and mobility improvements?
faqs.answer: The right number of sessions depends on how long the problem has been present, how restricted the tissue is, your activity level, and how your body responds. Acute tightness may improve within 1–3 sessions. Long-standing dysfunction may need 4–8 sessions, followed by maintenance care when recurring tension or movement restrictions need continued support.

faqs.question: Do I need to be an athlete to benefit from sports and deep tissue muscle therapy?
faqs.answer: No. Sports and deep tissue techniques are useful for anyone dealing with repetitive muscular stress, restricted movement, or persistent tightness. Desk workers may need help with neck, shoulder, back, or hip tension, while active adults can use targeted muscle therapy to improve mobility, recover between activities, and move with less restriction.

faqs.question: What should I expect after a session, and how should I prepare?
faqs.answer: Wear comfortable clothing, especially when stretching or corrective movement may be part of your session, and arrive normally hydrated. Mild tenderness or soreness can sometimes occur for 24–48 hours after deeper work. Keep movement comfortable afterward and avoid jumping straight into an intense workout if the treated tissues still feel sensitive.

faq.question: Does hot stone massage hurt, and how hot should the stones feel?
